sentences.text: The holotype fossil of Eocathayornis has been preserved only as impressions.
Zhou Zhonghe discovered the holotype in 1994 at the Boluochi quarry within the Jiufotang Formation.
Eocathayornis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
It is a genus of enantiornithean birds considered more basal or primitive than related genera like Sinornis and Cathayornis.
Zhou placed Eocathayornis in the family Cathayornithidae in 2002.
Eocathayornis is an extinct avialan belonging to the Enantiornithes clade that inhabited the Early Cretaceous in present-day China.
The time range for Eocathayornis is from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian.

Recent studies show the phylogenetic position of Eocathayornis is labile, varying between affiliations with Bohaiornithidae, basal positions near Pengornithidae, or advanced positions depending on included taxa.
A 2024 analysis supported a clade linking Cathayornis and Eocathayornis, though this was considered less comprehensive than a 2026 study.
